title: On the Indistinguishability of Human v/s AI Generated Text
abstract: arXiv:2608.26797v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The rapid improvement of LLMs has made distinguishing AI-generated text from human writing a pressing problem. This challenge is further amplified by paraphrasing tools designed to make machine-generated text appear more "human". We study how access to human writing samples can be used to strategically paraphrase machine-generated responses toward the human distribution. Under a multi-sample setting with human and machine responses to the same prompts, we show that repeated paraphrasing moves the machine distribution toward the empirical human distribution under simple mixing and stability conditions. Our results derive an explicit convergence rate, extend the analysis to a finite-sample setting, and characterize how the required number of human samples and paraphrasing rounds scale with the desired error.

translated_title: 论人类与AI生成文本的不可区分性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26797v1 公告类型：新 摘要：大型语言模型的快速进步使得区分AI生成文本与人类写作成为一个紧迫的问题。这一挑战因旨在让机器生成文本看起来更“人类化”的改写工具而进一步加剧。我们研究了如何利用人类写作样本，通过策略性改写机器生成响应，使其接近人类分布。在与相同提示的人类和机器响应多样本设置下，我们表明，在简单的混合和稳定性条件下，重复改写会使机器分布向经验人类分布移动。我们的结果推导出显式的收敛速率，将分析扩展到有限样本设置，并刻画了所需人类样本数量和改写轮次如何随期望误差变化。
tldr: 本文提出在多样本设置下，通过重复改写机器文本并利用人类样本，可证明其分布向人类分布收敛，并给出收敛速率和样本需求。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that under multi-sample settings, repeated paraphrasing with human samples can provably move machine text distribution toward human distribution, deriving convergence rates and sample requirements.
